scenes.question: For page authoring, which component references a Content Fragment on a page?
scenes.heading: The Content Fragment Component references the fragment on the page
scenes.body: The speech says that for page authoring, a fragment is referenced on a page with the Content Fragment Component, which is a core component.

scenes.question: Why does Adobe recommend keeping the number of Content Fragment models to a small set, usually at most low tens?
scenes.heading: Too many models slow GraphQL queries and complicate governance
scenes.body: The speech says to create as many models as needed but no more, and that too many slows GraphQL queries and complicates governance.

scenes.question: What is the recommended limit for deep nesting of Content Fragment References?
scenes.heading: Keep Content Fragment Reference nesting to no more than ten levels
scenes.body: The speech says to avoid deep nesting of Content Fragment References and to keep nesting to no more than ten levels.

scenes.question: Why should a Content Fragment avoid having more than ten variations?
scenes.heading: More than ten variations add processing time on author and on delivery
scenes.body: The speech says not to exceed ten variations per fragment because variations add processing time on author and on delivery.
